title: RAF Moscow live blog: Khamzat Chimaev vs. Tyron Woodley
description: Two former UFC champs battle in the RAF Moscow headliner
fullText:
This is the RAF Moscow live blog for Khamzat Chimaev vs. Tyron Woodley, the 195-pound catchweight main event for Saturday's card in Russia.

Chimaev makes his second appearance in the promotion since losing the UFC middleweight title to Sean Strickland at UFC 328 in May. In his Real American Freestyle debut, Chimaev pinned Dillon Danis in under a minute at RAF 10 in June, which then led to an all-out brawl between the two teams. "Borz" is set to compete a second time in a less than two-week span as he's slated to face Gilbert Burns at RAF 13 on Sept. 18 in Miami.

Woodley recently competed at RAF 12 in August and picked up a comeback victory against current UFC welterweight Joaquin Buckley. The former UFC welterweight champion earned his first combat sports victory in nearly eight years following a seven-fight skid — which includes a slew of UFC bouts, along with three boxing bouts against Jake Paul and Anderson Silva.

Check out the Chimaev vs. Woodley live blog below.

Depending on which book you look at, Khamzat Chimaev is anywhere from a -5000 to -10000 favorite, while Tyron Woodley comes back between a +812 to +2000 underdog. Not a lot of faith in "The Chosen One."

Tyron Woodley makes his way to the mat and is moving quickly. He looks ready to go. Now the lights go out, a la The Undertaker, and the camera man perfectly shoots a man picking his nose in the crowd. Chimaev is on the mat and the official intros are about to take place.

Chimaev shakes Woodley's hand after he's intro'd, and we're off. They lock up nd Chimaev looks so much bigger in there. Woodley shoots a single, Chimaev scrambles around the back with an ankle pick and the ref blows the whistle. Back to the feet they go. Chimaev pushes Woodley over the line to get the first point of the match.

Chimaev gets another push out to make it 2-0 and we're back at it. Woodley shoots again, thwarted by Chimaev. "Borz" gets a full body lock and slams Tyron to the mat, then Chimaev gets the shoulders to the mat and gets the pin! Just like that, it's over!

Chimaev is now speaking to Chael Sonnen, who is talking about his t-shirt that features the late Buvaisar Saitiev. Chimaev is now 2-0 with two pinfalls in RAF and when he's asked what he wants in the future, Chimaev says whoever, as he's already set to face Gilbert Burns on Sept. 18 in Miami at RAF 13.

And that's it for RAF Moscow. 13 matches in a little over three hours.

title: 'That's a sackable performance' - what next for Martin at Leicester?
description: Tipped for a turnaround in fortunes, the Foxes and their boss continue to falter in the third tier.
fullText:
"I don't think the manager should get sacked tonight, but that is a sackable performance."

Russell Martin's Leicester City slumped to a new depths on Saturday when they were hammered 4-0 at home by Oxford United, conceding three second-half goals in just 20 minutes.

It was their heaviest-ever defeat in the third tier and marked an all-time low in the club's otherwise proud 142-year history, despondent fans told BBC Radio Leicester at full-time.

Not long ago the Foxes were the darlings of English football, a living fairytale after their 2015-16 Premier League title win against all odds.

Many had expected them to stroll through League One after their unexpected relegation last term - their second in as many seasons - but life back in the third tier under the divisive Martin has been far more difficult than envisaged.

Granted, it is still early days, but those who watch the club regularly are already concerned.

"This manager doesn't seem to want to move away, at all, from the pass them to death, that's how we will win a football match," says former Leicester player and BBC Radio Leicester match summariser Matt Piper.

"I'm an advocate of that style when your team is playing well and can execute it in the way that you want it. I'm also an advocate of winning football matches and you can do that in many different ways.

"We have only seen one way from this manager. My fingers are pointing at him this afternoon, even though the team didn't play well.

"I don't think the manager should get sacked tonight, but that is a sackable performance."

Martin is already under pressure from sections of the club's fanbase, who made their feelings clear during Saturday's defeat.

Oxford Utd thump Leicester to heap pressure on Martin

Martin's reputation on line as he tries to halt Leicester slide

After five league games, he has just one win with two draws and two defeats.

Following a disastrous spell at Rangers, which lasted just 123 days, and his sacking from Southampton, with whom he earned just one win in 16 Premier League games after leading them to promotion, he too is in need of a revival.

While disappointed with the performance against Oxford, which followed an impressive 2-0 midweek win over potential promotion rivals Plymouth Argyle, he remained steadfast in his commitment to the project at the King Power Stadium.

"I'm not concerned about that happening again," he told BBC Radio Leicester.

"I feel I understand what's happened today with so many young guys and a tough moment. We can't quite get through it and after a big, busy period.

"We will be better for it. We have a week now and we have to make sure we put it right next week."

The Foxes started Saturday's game with five players in the starting XI under the age of 23, including two teenagers.

Their five substitutions were aged 18, 19, 20, 21 and 23.

The number of arrivals and departures at the club since their relegation are both well into double figures.

The club, which is also up for sale, is very much in a period of transition.

Martin rued his side's "naivety and inexperience" in their latest defeat, adding: "We had a lot of players who were doing a third game in a week for the first time in their careers, but it's not an excuse.

"But I think that's the learning now - we have to find a team on the pitch, especially in a three-game week that can deliver a consistent level of aggression and a consistent level of energy because the last three games we have built so much energy, so much feel-good factor about it.

"The players and staff, the fans have been brilliant and we had to build on the win on Tuesday night and today we have done the opposite."

There is a genuine uncertainty about whether Martin will be given the time to try to put things right after such a damaging defeat, as Piper explains.

"If you look back over the years, especially at this football club at managers that we have sacked, that looked like a manager that could get sacked tonight."

title: "I did what the team asked": Kimi Antonelli expects George Russell to return favour later in season
description: With a grid penalty compromising his own Monza weekend, Kimi Antonelli focused on helping title rival George Russell in qualifying - and expects the favour to be returned
fullText:
After helping George Russell with a tow in Monza qualifying, Kimi Antonelli says he expects his team-mate and championship rival to act in the same way later in the season.

The Italian had little to gain from his own qualifying result because of a back-of-the-grid penalty and effectively spent the session helping Russell, who ultimately qualified second.

Mercedes took the opportunity to install new engine components in Antonelli's car at Monza, given it is one of the easier tracks on the calendar for overtaking and the team needed to expand his pool of available power unit components.

It meant the championship leader had a different job at his home track: helping his team-mate and closest title rival in the fight for pole position.

That included assisting Russell on both of his Q3 runs. Antonelli ran ahead of his team-mate at the start of the laps to give him a slipstream down the main straight before letting Russell through.

Russell ultimately benefited from the arrangement and earned second place on the grid, behind Pierre Gasly, who claimed his maiden F1 pole position.

"Obviously it's a very weird feeling," Antonelli said of his unusual Saturday afternoon. "I had to do my job, which was to help George. I tried my best in order to help as much as possible."

Antonelli's only attempt of his own in Q3 came on an almost empty track in the middle of the session. Having given Russell a tow, he continued for another lap and posted a time good enough for seventh in the session.

His qualifying position ultimately mattered little, as he will start the race from the back of the grid because of his penalty for exceeding his permitted allocation of power unit components – something that was already known before the start of the weekend.

"Q3 was very weird, even the lap I did," he said. "It was an OK lap, but nothing special. I had more fuel in the car than what you normally would have. I didn't want to do any mistakes that would compromise the program that we had planned, which was to give the slipstream to George in the last lap as well. Obviously mixed feelings, but it's what it is. We're ready to fight tomorrow."

How Oscar Piastri's Q3 mistake denied Lando Norris "half a second" in Italian GP qualifying

Despite both Mercedes drivers being involved in the title fight, the team has been adamant that Russell and Antonelli must act in the team's interests first and foremost, including accepting team orders when required to maximise its result.

Russell did exactly that two weeks ago at Zandvoort. Antonelli had been running ahead of him before making a late pit stop under the virtual safety car, which dropped him behind Russell but left him on fresher tyres. Mercedes subsequently instructed Russell to let Antonelli through, and he complied despite initially questioning the call.

At Monza, it was Antonelli's turn to play the team game. And with Russell also expected to need additional power unit components later in the season, Antonelli expects his team-mate to return the favour if the opportunity arises.

"We're all aligned on this," he said. "As he's been a good team player in Zandvoort, I did what the team asked me to do. I'm happy that it worked out.

"Of course, when it's his turn, we're going to talk about it. We're very clear on that. When we can, we will help each other, especially in this kind of situation. I had nothing to win and he was fighting for pole."

With Russell trailing Antonelli in the championship by 59 points, Monza presents him with a good opportunity to close the gap because of his team-mate's penalty.

Yet it remains unclear whether Antonelli will need to take further engine components later in the year, with Mercedes working on an upgraded engine. The best opportunity for Russell to clear his own penalties could be Baku, another track on the calendar where overtaking is considered relatively easy.

title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili: Live blog, round-by-round and results
description: Katie Taylor’s farewell fight at Croke Park is LIVE today!
fullText:
Katie Taylor will fight for the final time today, saying goodbye to boxing in front of 80,000 fans at Dublin's Croke Park, in a main event against Flora Pili for the super lightweight undisputed championship.

Taylor's farewell promises to be an emotional night of pageantry and richly-deserved praise, and she'll hope it ends with becoming a three-time undisputed world champion.

Patrick Stumberg will lead the call today for us, with round-by-round updates for the main event, and fight-by-fight updates and results for the undercard. Join us!

Post-Fight Thoughts: One-way traffic for Donovan (16-2, 12 KO, as expected. Just way too sharp for McKenna (25-7-1, 8 KO), who found his offense completely neutered by Donovan's technical superiority. Donovan sent him to a knee with a counter right to the body in the second, took his foot off the gas for a bit in the third, then ramped up again in the fourth to open a nasty, fight-ending cut above McKenna's right eye. Donovan heads into a title shot against Liam Paro and the 36-year-old McKenna is left to consider his future after another high-profile defeat.

McKenna whooping but offering little else in the fourth. Donovan stalking, landing heavy shots, splits McKenna open with a sharp left hand. The doctor takes one look at it and immediately calls the fight. McKenna TKO-4.

McKenna showing a bit more life and Donovan staying measured.

Fade-back right hook to the body puts McKenna down on a delayed reaction in the second. Donovan stalking.

Three minutes in and Donovan's already sitting down on his combinations. Don't feel like this lasts long.

Preview: Donovan (15-2, 11 KO) getting what should be a layup after two controversial losses to Lewis Crocker and a gritty majority decision over Karen Chukhadzhian. He's theoretically got a shot at Liam Paro in his pocket should he get past McKenna (25-6-1, 8 KO), who's dropped three of his last five.

Post-Fight Thoughts: Phenomenal performance from Bevan (10-0, 9 KO) against former Olympian Brennan (6-1, 1 KO). They spent virtually the entire fight forehead to forehead, with Bevan's superior sharpness, output, and power keeping him in the driver's seat throughout. Tons of potential at just 25; he's got the shot selection and overall composure of a mature, complete fighter. Gutting for Brennan, who never gave up but just found himself completely outgunned and let down by his corner.

Beautiful body combo and this time Brennan goes down face-first. He tries to attack and gets absolutely melted by a right hook, crikey. Bevan KO-6

Liver shot and Brennan's down again at the end of the fifth! Looks done but beats the count and heads to his corner.

Bevan looking razor-sharp today. Great punch selection, mixing speeds, never getting irresponsible with his defense.

Gnarly left hook sits down Brennan at the end of the third and a nasty right hand discombobulates him at the bell! He makes it to his corner but he does not look like he's in fighting shape.

Solid back-and-forth action through two. Bevan mixing levels well, Brennan looking to catch and pitch.

title: Glasner and Williams dispute VAR call over Forest handball
description: Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner and Neco Williams believe VAR should not have ruled out defender's goal against Tottenham.
fullText:
Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner claimed the video assistant referee (VAR) was "guessing" and should not have intervened in ruling out Neco Williams' goal in their 0-0 draw with Tottenham.

Williams' second-half effort was chalked off with the full-back adjudged to have bundled the ball in with his arm after some calamitous Tottenham defending at the City Ground.

The Forest defender denied it came off his arm and insisted it should have stood.

Initially, referee Craig Pawson awarded the goal but VAR Peter Bankes intervened.

"I watched five or six different angles and, to be fair, from one angle you can guess that the ball touched the arm because the shirt moves a little bit, but it's not clear is it the ball or [Sandro] Tonali on the goalline," said Glasner.

"I think the VAR can't intervene when he is guessing. It was not clear and obvious.

"We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high, which is why this is a wrong intervention.

"If it's not 100% clear, stick to the on-field decisions. This is the inconsistency today.

"I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood."

The Premier League's official match centre posted on their X page the explanation as to why it was ruled out following the incident in the 67th minute.

It stated: "VAR checked the referee's call of goal to Nottingham Forest - and determined that Williams handled the ball immediately before scoring and recommended that the goal was disallowed."

The rule states that if the ball has hit the arm of the goalscorer immediately before they score then it must be ruled out, even if accidental.

However, Williams denied that it struck his arm amid the chaos in the Spurs box.

"It's a goal," the Forest full-back told Sky Sports.

"VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I've seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it. I headed it in between my arms.

"I knew straight away I've headed it down in between my arms. At a loss at that one. Disappointing."

'Not Football Manager' - De Zerbi says misfiring Spurs need time

The biggest issue with judging handball is often determining if the ball did actually hit the arm, and that is the crux of Forest's argument.

Williams is adamant the ball came off his head and did not touch his hand, evidence which of course would not be available to the VAR.

Even having a chip in the ball, like at the World Cup, would not help here as the head and hands were so close together.

This is not about a clear and obvious error, as that covers subjective incidents like potential penalties.

It is a factual overturn so the VAR, Bankes, is looking for definitive proof. This is similar but without taking into account what the referee, Pawson, says he has seen.

Definitive proof can be seen as a higher bar than clear and obvious, because it is a factual decision - that the ball definitely touched the goalscorer's arm.

Glasner, Williams and most of the Forest fanbase refuse to accept that evidence does exist, and that there were no grounds to disallow the goal.

These decisions come down to one factor - the judgement of who is in the VAR room on a given match.

It is unavoidable that another VAR on a different day might feel the threshold of proof had not been crossed, and allow the goal to stand.

And this will always be one of the major frustrations with VAR.

Harry Maguire's goal against Ipswich last weekend was allowed despite a handball because his shot was going wide before it was deflected, meaning it was an own goal.

In the Williams' case, he actually was the goalscorer so any touch on the arm means the goal must be ruled out.

The only thing that would have saved the goal was if the ball had fully crossed the line before it was kicked against Williams.

title: Yankees place Trent Grisham on IL with hamstring strain, recall Jasson Domínguez
description: The Yankees’ center fielder will miss some time after being pulled from Friday night’s game.
fullText:
The Yankees lost in walk-off fashion to San Diego on Friday night, but they might not have played extras had it not been for a misplay that allowed the Padres to score their only run of the initial nine innings. With two outs in the second, Xander Bogaerts got under a pitch from Max Fried on what could charitably be described as a flare to center. It was a ball that most center fielder would've at minimum come close to and have the chance for a diving catch.

But for the Yankees, Trent Grisham was in center field, and while he was once an elite defender, he has been far from that in 2026. It didn't help that he was playing a guy with an 82 OPS+ and only 11 homers far too deep, but regardless, he was clearly not moving well on the play. The ball dipped in with ease and Ty France scored. When the half-inning ended, Grisham spoke to the team trainer and disappeared down the dugout tunnel. Soon, the Yankees announced that Grisham was dealing with discomfort in his right hamstring, the same one that sent him to the IL earlier in 2026. It's been an uneven year on the whole for Grisham, who has hit .211/.308/.395 with 18 homers but only a 95 OPS+.

Now, we know that Grisham is indeed heading back to the IL. Jasson Domínguez will fly from Scranton to San Diego to rejoin the team and take Grisham's spot on the roster. The former top prospect had an injury of his own earlier in 2026, but when given the chance to play, he did not acquit himself well, batting just .230/.270/.380 with a 79 OPS+ and exactly 0.0 rWAR.

It might only be a short-term stay for Domínguez since it seems like Aaron Judge is tracking to return to the team soon (though New York has made no announcements) and there's only so much roster flexibility at the moment. But for now, Domínguez will serve as outfield depth, though Spencer Jones will likely get the lion's share of time in center with Grisham out. Cody Bellinger is a candidate for some center field time as well, though he did bang himself up a bit on a foul ball last night too.

Prior to today’s game, the Yankees made the following roster moves:
•Placed OF Trent Grisham on the 10-day injured list with a right hamstring strain.
•Recalled OF Jasson Domínguez (#24) from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre.

title: Springboks edge fiery clash against New Zealand to edge 2-1 ahead in series
description: South Africa won the third of four Tests while New Zealand captain Ardie Savea was forced off and is a doubt for the final clash
fullText:
South Africa edged another ferocious and bruising clash against New Zealand to win the third Test 29-24 on Saturday and go 2-1 up in the four-Test Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series.

Both teams scored ⁠four tries in front of 87,976 fans at Soccer City, with the Springboks coming back after trailing in the first half to add to their narrow success in last weekend's second test in Cape Town.

It ⁠proved another classic contest of Springbok forward power against the All Blacks' pacey passing attack, with New Zealand starting furiously but ​eventually being ⁠worn down by the physicality of their hosts.

Ardie Savea went off nine minutes before halftime with a shoulder injury in a blow to the tourists and he looks uncertain for the final match, which will be played in Baltimore, in the United States, next Saturday.

Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus said: "It was epic and intense, fierce battle in all departments. The scoreboard in the end showed how close it was. Were just happy to win."

His Kiwi counterpart Dave Rennie said: "There was not a lot in it. They were probably ‌stronger than they had been in the first two tests. I'm really proud ‌but we have to be better at the discipline stuff which gives them easy entries. The change room is pretty gutted but our mindset will be to bounce next week."

The All Blacks' opening try came in the 11th minute from a quick lineout that saw Asafo Aumua storm at the home defence and Savea pick up possession to burst over.

South Africa responded 10 minutes later, moving the ball down the line with a handoff from Damian de Allende setting up wing Kurt-Lee Arendse to dive over in the corner. But five minutes later, Savea was at it again, picking up a loose ball to go over from close range after Leroy Carter had slipped tackles to burst down the left wing.

South Africa pulled level four minutes before the break with a penalty try after scrumming the All Blacks back over their own goal-line to make it 12-12 at halftime.

Will Jordan was a constant threat off the wing, and his ​kick through 15 minutes into the second half fell perfectly for the chasing Carter, who was tackled short of the ‌line but managed to sit up the ball for ⁠Jordan to sprint on to and extend his try-scoring record to 54.

The home response was almost immediate as Carter went from hero to villain, missing his tackle and allowing Jesse Kriel an open avenue to romp to the try line from outside the 22 and dot down.

Springbok forward power ‌then extended the lead with a maul ​that advanced them over 20 metres to the tryline, allowing Malcolm Marx ‌to go over in the 66th minute.

A Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulus penalty with 10 minutes to go put them 12 points ahead and effectively sealed the result, although Samisoni Taukeiaho reduced the advantage with a try on the final whistle.

title: ESPN says Panthers' biggest X factor in 2026 is also their biggest unknown
description: Could a big unknown for the Panthers also be their biggest X factor in 2026? This ESPN analyst thinks so . . .
fullText:
The 2026 season is lining up to be a career-defining moment for Carolina Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks.

ESPN's Ben Solak recently named each NFL team's X factor going into the upcoming campaign. For Carolina, he lists Brooks—who he also describes as the team's "biggest unknown" at the moment:

The Panthers appear to have a budding star in second-year receiver Tetairoa McMillan, and Jalen Coker is a fine running mate. But Carolina desperately needs another explosive weapon to emerge on offense if it is going to successfully build around quarterback Bryce Young's skill set. Brooks was drafted to be the dominant drumbeat as a 20-plus-carry player and the home run threat on quick passes and screens that Canales has always schemed up well. If we finally get to see the player who has been promised, it'll move the needle on Carolina's season.

Thanks to a pair of ACL tears, Brooks has been unable to even try to move any sort of needle as a pro. Since being selected in the second round of the 2024 draft, he's appeared in only three regular-season games—all of which came in his rookie season.

Brooks nearly matched that total this summer, having played in the first two preseason games of his NFL career. In limited action over two contests, he rushed for 23 on eight carries and added nine receiving yards on one catch.

Time will tell if Brooks becomes the drumbeat Solak alludes to, as the Panthers still value the presence of sixth-year veteran Chuba Hubbard. But if Brooks turns up as the prospect the organization drafted him to be, then the backfield could turn into his show.

title: Danny Parkins drops a bombshell trade prediction for Raiders
description: The Dallas Cowboys’ total cap space has crossed $33 million, fueling rumors of a blockbuster trade for Las Vegas Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys have restructured the contracts of three veteran players, Kenny Clark, DaRon Bland, and Jake Ferguson, giving the team an immediate $19 million in cap space. After this big financial restructuring, the Cowboys' total cap space has crossed $33 million, fueling rumors of a blockbuster trade for Las Vegas Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby.

DJ Cabanlong - The Sporting Tribune

Las Vegas Raiders defensive-end Maxx Crosby stretches alongside the warm up lines during Raiders OTAs at Intermountain Health Performance Center, Wednesday May 20, 2026 in Henderson, Nev.

On Friday, 'The Herd with Colin Cowherd' talk show host Danny Parkins explained that this trade will definitely happen before the Week 10 deadline.

"I anticipate that Maxx Crosby is going to be a Cowboy before the trade deadline, which is week 10," Parkins said. "I don't see any reason for Maxx Crosby to be a Raider. They tried to trade him for the Ravens. The Ravens flunked him on his physical. Other teams like the Cowboys, Bears, and others had been in on the pursuit of Maxx Crosby."

According to Parkins, the September games will be a big platform for Crosby to prove his fitness.

"I think that September is an audition for Maxx Crosby for the rest of the league. Crosby looks healthy. Crosby is productive… I think Maxx Crosby is a cowboy by the end of this season," he added.

The Cowboys had made trade offers three times before, which the Raiders had rejected. The most serious talks happened in March this year, when the Raiders had accepted a trade package from the Baltimore Ravens, but the deal fell through at the last moment. Dallas owner Jerry Jones clarified while talking about these failed negotiations:

"We did not walk away," Jones said. "That's about all there is to say. We understood his injury well. We thought he could help us then. We were surprised by the way that was resolved. To interject anything about what we're thinking or doing, because he went back to the Raiders, would be a mistake. He's a Raider."

Last November, the Cowboys inquired about Crosby for the first time, but after the Raiders declined, they had to trade Quinnen Williams. After that, this March, Dallas offered their No. 12 pick and a 2027 second-rounder, but the Raiders preferred the Ravens' offer of two first-round picks.

The Ravens had backed out of the trade on March 10 due to a degenerative issue in Crosby's left knee. However, Crosby stayed in Las Vegas and is now fully recovered, after which the Cowboys have made these big financial adjustments.

Now with over $33 million in cap space, the Cowboys have the full financial power to handle Crosby's $30 million base salary. Between the veteran quarterback, Dak Prescott, owner Jerry Jones in his early 80s, and the team's 30-plus year Super Bowl drought, the team is now in 'win now' mode by betting on future draft assets. Parkins said about this:

"That's the exact situation to mortgage a little bit of the future. Like, trade a draft pick to go get a player. So I think Maxx Crosby's going to be a Cowboy,"

If the Raiders struggle under their new defensive coordinator Rob Leonard, trade talks will pick up fast. On the other hand, Raiders owner Mark Davis has completely dismissed the possibilities of a trade. Davis gave a forceful statement last season:

"It's really hard to keep getting asked the same question every month or week or whatever when the answer's going to stay the same. I don't know why anybody would think I'd change my mind or the organization would."

This aggressive contract restructuring by the Cowboys shows their desperate attempt to capitalize on the championship window before Pickens' contract expires next year. After trading superstar Micah Parsons to Green Bay, Jerry Jones is now fully ready to risk tomorrow in order to win today.

title: NASCAR expands adjustments that O'Reilly teams can make in practice
description: Teams had more options when trying to improve their cars in practice at Darlington Raceway
fullText:
NASCAR is expanding practice adjustments for NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series teams at Darlington Raceway this weekend by adding rear springs to the list of allowed changes during practice.

NASCAR teams have a limited list of adjustments that are allowed during practice sessions and since practice was condensed during the Covid-19 pandemic, that list has prevented most parts from being swapped and limited adjustments on others.

The typical adjustments that have been allowed over the last few years are similar to those that might be completed during a pit stop, such as adjusting tire pressures or adjusting a trackbar/shock using the adjuster wrench through the window.

Removing or replacing parts has mostly been outlawed over the past few years, especially at the rear of the car. Practice sessions in the NASCAR O'Reilly Series were expanded to 50 minutes at the start of the year but the limited adjustment rules remained, which limited how much teams could actually benefit from the second set of tires if they chose to use them. The NASCAR Cup Series followed with a similar extension, starting at New Hampshire Motor Speedway a few weeks ago, but their allowed adjustments list did not expand outside of an additional tire set.

NASCAR has allowed the rear springs to be changed in the NASCAR O'Reilly Series a couple of times this year, but it was mostly due to special circumstances like the use of resin and the tire dragon at Dover. The fact that it's being allowed at Darlington Raceway along with the extra set of tires appears to signal that they're willing to be more flexible with practice, which is a positive change.

The change was welcomed when checking in with a variety of personnel in the garage ranging from competition personnel to team leadership, as most saw it as an opportunity to use parts they already own to help them make their cars better. Teams that don't have significant simulation resources see it as something that they can grasp as well, allowing them to get closer to the front end of the field.

Allowing rear spring changes will now allow teams to have a wider window of adjustment outside of just adding or removing springs rubbers to tweak rate in small increments. This will give teams more opportunities to tweak a setup and not be solely reliant on hitting the correct spring combination during simulator prep ahead of a race weekend. Well-resourced teams at the top end of the grid will always see benefits from any added adjustments but this change will also help some of the smaller teams on the grid without huge additional cost. This will be significant at a track like Darlington where a right rear spring change can significantly impact how a car turns and teams won't be stuck with what they installed at the shop.

Should teams be allowed to change brake pads? 👀@BoziTatarevic breaks down how NASCAR and IMSA differ when it comes to parts changes and how to get a competitive edge.

Watch the full episode of NASCAR Inside the Race: https://t.co/zd8Qo431lr pic.twitter.com/gxXd3bj9n9

On a recent episode of NASCAR Inside The Race, I discussed how practice could be improved to make teams more competitive and one of the examples we used was spring changes and how much of an impact they have during IMSA practice where they are allowed.

Crew chief Todd Gordon suggested that NASCAR could allow Cup Series teams to bring multiple sets of shocks to be inspected and sealed during a race weekend so that they could have more spring options and just be reliant on incremental changes to the single set of springs that they pick.

The allowance of rear springs change for NASCAR O'Reilly Series teams this weekend is a step in that direction and the learnings from that could pave a path for additional adjustments and parts changes to be allowed in Cup or Truck Series in the future.

title: Bayern Munich drops points to Schalke for the first time in almost a decade
description: FC Bayern did not do enough vs. Schalke to get a win.
fullText:
Bayern Munich dropped points against Schalke for the first time since 2017 per @iMiaSanMia), as the newly promoted side held the defending champions to a 0-0 draw at the VELTINS-Arena. The result ended Bayern's run of 10 consecutive victories over Schalke.

It was a frustrating evening for Vincent Kompany's team. Bayern Munich controlled the majority of possession and created several opportunities, but Schalke's compact defensive setup proved extremely difficult to break down. Loris Karius was particularly impressive in goal, producing several important saves to preserve his clean sheet.

Kompany initially started Harry Kane and Michael Olise on the bench, while Jamal Musiala also began among the substitutes as Bayern looked to manage their attacking options. The game changed somewhat after Kane, Olise and Musiala were introduced, but Bayern still could not find the breakthrough. Musiala's return was nevertheless a major positive, as he made his comeback after his recent health issues.

Schalke deserves massive credit. Playing its first Bundesliga home match in more than three years,Schalke defended with discipline, competed for every ball and secured a point that will feel like a victory.

For Bayern Munich, however, it is two points dropped. After opening the season with a dominant 5-1 victory over VfB Stuttgart, the champions leave Gelsenkirchen frustrated — and no longer perfect.

fullText:
We will have plenty more to say per usual, but Alabama took care of business in the opener. Keelon Russell commanded the offense well and made some spectacular plays, but also tried to get a bit greedy on a few occasions and it could have bitten him. He will need to learn the concept of taking profit as this level.

Trae'shawn Brown and EJ Crowell look the part, and Ryan Coleman-Williams shook off two early drops to have a great afternoon. Lotzeir Brooks made perhaps the play of the game in the fourth quarter with a dazzling catch and run when he looked to be bottled up near the sideline.

Lotzeir Brooks very Dante Hall like pic.twitter.com/UlPmNgOnre

title: Ryan Coleman-Williams has ups and downs in Alabama football opener | Goodbread
description: Alabama football WR Ryan Coleman-Williams made some big plays and a couple blunders in the Crimson Tide's season-opening win over East Carolina.
fullText:
Alabama football opened the season with a resounding victory over East Carolina, 48-10 on Saturday, Sept. 5 at Bryant-Denny Stadium, to begin coach Kalen DeBoer's third season leading the Crimson Tide. The Pirates were outmanned from the outset, and Alabama had no trouble securing the win despite significant offseason changes to its offensive staff and personnel. Here are a few instant observations from UA's 2026 lid-lifter.

1) Keelon Russell showed very well for his first career start at quarterback. Apart from an ill-advised throw in the first quarter that was nearly intercepted, the sophomore's decision-making was poised, his passing was accurate and his athleticism was obvious. Alabama has a dynamic young talent. And while East Carolina wasn't exactly a stiff test, it's not as if Russell had all day to throw. He didn't. One lone quibble − Russell doesn't appear to be much for sliding at the end of runs; expect the UA coaching staff to counsel him about self-preservation.

HIGHLIGHTS: Alabama vs East Carolina live updates: Score, highlights, analysis

SCOTT OUT: Alabama football WR Rico Scott exits ECU game: What we know on apparent injury

2) The UA defense is more ready for SEC play than the offense. The inside linebackers, among the defense's only preseason question marks, played quite well. The pass rush couldn't be judged as fairly, because the Pirates' passing offense got rid of the ball, for the most part, eye-blink quick. ECU did take advantage of a coverage hiccup for a 68-yard completion that set up a touchdown, but secondary play was otherwise tight, especially with the first unit on the field.

3) What to make of Ryan Coleman-Williams' season debut? It only took him a half to ring up 100 yards receiving, so of course, he checked the big-play box as always. But the drops that haunted him in 2025 returned as well; one for what would've been a big play in the first quarter, and another at the front corner of the end zone that was scrubbed by an ECU penalty. Then there was a botched exchange on a handoff to Coleman-Williams in the second half, on which he clearly expected Russell to pull the ball, resulting in Alabama's only turnover.

Pick your touchdown here, but after allowing ECU to cut the lead to 17-7, Alabama's offense answered immediately with a six-play, 86-yard touchdown drive, highlighted by a 58-yard reception by Coleman-Williams. RB Daniel Hill punched in a 2-yard score to finish the possession, dashing the only moment of momentum East Carolina had all day.

335 - That was Russell's combined yardage for passing and rushing.

Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer's decision to stick with Russell at quarterback well into the fourth quarter was the right move. While it can be argued that, from an injury standpoint, it would've been wise to put backup Austin Mack in the game sooner, Russell still needed as many live-game snaps as possible. In advance of Russell's first SEC start, a road test at Kentucky, DeBoer chose to give his quarterback a little more action, a little more tape to study and a little more of a learning opportunity.

Signs that this offensive line isn't ready for primetime were everywhere. ECU's defensive front got too much penetration against both run and pass, but couldn't finish a number of plays that an SEC defense would have. Too often, running backs were fighting traffic right from the handoff. Russell was sacked just once, but credit his escapeability, not his protection, for that.

title: Alabama report card: Grading the Crimson Tide after rolling through ECU
description: How did Alabama football do against East Carolina? We hand out grades for the offense, defense, coaching, special teams and overall performance.
fullText:
Alabama football wanted to make a statement in its first test of the 2026 season — and at some points, the Crimson Tide did.

The veteran defense looked ready for the rigors of SEC play. First-time starting quarterback Keelon Russell was exciting, elusive and explosive for an offense that, at its best, moved the ball consistently downfield.

But in Alabama's 48-10 win against East Carolina, the Crimson Tide showed its share of highs and lows.

Here's our postgame report card after Alabama's win against East Carolina:

ALABAMA vs EAST CAROLINA: Alabama vs East Carolina live updates: Score, highlights, analysis

KEELON RUSSELL: Live stats for Keelon Russell in first start for Alabama football vs ECU

Keelon Russell made it incredibly clear why he was picked as Alabama's starting quarterback, showing extreme elusiveness and explosiveness along with consistency moving the ball downfield. The run game is much better, too, with Daniel Hill, EJ Crowell and Russell finding daylight and falling forward and through East Carolina defenders. The Crimson Tide showed bumps along the way, whether it was Russell running for his life and taking hits or Ryan Coleman-Williams' drops and a fumble, despite an overall solid performance statistically. That was the first half. The second brought inconsistencies and an inability to move the ball until Trae'shawn Brown's 2-yard touchdown run on the first play of the fourth quarter to make the score 44-10. This is an offense that isn't a finished product and nowhere near perfect, but there was enough to show potential, potential that can be groundbreaking in the long run.

Other than one busted play that led to East Carolina's only touchdown, Alabama's defense was dominant, forcing the Pirates off the field and creating turnovers, headlined by Yhonzae Pierre's first career interception, one he returned for a score. Alabama's defense looks SEC-ready, one that continues to rotate fresh bodies in without much of a dropoff.

Saturday brought no questions about Conor Talty and Alabama's kicking game, Alex Asparuhov hit two 50-plus-yard punts and the most talked-about part of the return game was that Ryan Coleman-Williams and Dijon Lee Jr. were the ones returning.

In an offseason defined by run game improvements, from the hires of Adrian Klemm and Richard Owens to a brand new offensive line, there was significant improvement, especially when compared to a season ago against Florida State. It's emblematic of Alabama's season debut: a group of coaches prioritizing and showing what their players had worked on all offseason, a showcase of a team that developed even if it's not a finished product.

Alabama's debut was not perfect by any means, but there was enough pointing in the right direction for the Crimson Tide to leave Bryant-Denny Stadium satisfied.

Yhonzae Pierre entered 2026 with ample expectation. From taking his first career interception for a score to securing his first sack of the season, Pierre began the season exactly how he needed to — by dominating.

title: Canadiens Likely to Keep $33.3 Million Star Amid Trade Links
description: The Montreal Canadiens are being urged not to trade away a highly rated defenseman to help land a new forward. The post Canadiens Likely to Keep $33.3 Million Star Amid Trade Links appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Montreal Canadiens general manager Kent Hughes remains interested in making a significant trade. The club has been repeatedly linked with a top-six forward, including Columbus Blue Jackets star Kirill Marchenko. While Hughes and the Canadiens would love to strike a deal, they obviously have to give up quality assets to complete the trade.

It was previously revealed that Montreal would be willing to part ways with high-profile prospects to land a current NHL star. Adam Engström and Alexander Zharovsky have both been specifically named as trade bait. Nevertheless, teams like the Blue Jackets are more likely to want NHL-ready players in a deal. Because of this, the Canadiens may have to dangle someone like Kaiden Guhle.

Montreal Gazette's Stu Cowan was asked if the Montreal Canadiens should trade the highly rated defenseman on the most recent episode of The Sick Podcast. "I think you hold on to him," replied Cowan. "I wrote a column a couple of weeks ago with his quotes from the end of the season, and he was outstanding in the playoffs. He's built for playoff hockey."

"There are players who get you to the playoffs, and players who get you through the playoffs. Kaiden Guhle is a guy who can get you through the playoffs," continued Cowan. "He was MVP of the Western Hockey League playoffs the year he led his team to the WHL championship. He plays that physical style of play the Canadiens need."

The Montreal Canadiens clearly rate Guhle fairly high. After all, Hughes and Co. rewarded the blueliner with a six-year, $33.3 million contract ($5.55 million AAV) in 2024. This came after the defenseman recorded 22 points in 70 games during the 2023-24 season. Although he had a solid campaign that year, he has yet to eclipse this point total or game tally in recent seasons.

As Cowan pointed out, Guhle has dealt with a series of unfortunate injuries during his time with Montreal. Some of these issues have been downright bizarre. For instance, the blueliner missed 21 games in 2025 after accidentally cutting himself with his own skate. He also had to have his appendix removed and most recently spent time on the sidelines due to a partially torn adductor muscle.

On top of these setbacks, the Montreal Canadiens also have a positional logjam in defense. More specifically, Hughes has a plethora of left-handed blueliners, including Guhle. At the moment, Guhle is projected to be a third-line pairing alongside Alexandre Carrier for the 2026-27 season.

While the Montreal Canadiens could be open to easing their defensive logjam, Guhle appears set to stay with the club. Shedding the blueliner's $5.5 million AAV contract would potentially benefit Hughes. Nevertheless, Montreal is not necessarily in a bad place financially. According to PuckPedia.com, the Canadiens have nearly $10 million in projected cap space.

Montreal still has to figure out what to do with RFAs Zack Bolduc and Arber Xhekaj. Bolduc, however, is widely expected to sign an extension with the Canadiens. Xhekaj, on the other hand, may be used in a trade to help land a star forward. Hughes rates the enforcer, but he is looking for ample playing time as a left-sided defenseman.

title: Texans GM Nick Caserio Draws Attention With Move on Local-Product QB
description: The Houston Texans are well-represented with general manager Nick Caserio taking matters into his own hands. The post Texans GM Nick Caserio Draws Attention With Move on Local-Product QB appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Sixth-year general manager Nick Caserio and the Houston Texans are working diligently, even during the team's break. First, reports emerged that the Texans would be on hand for the Ohio State Buckeyes season-opener against Ball State.

It appears, though, that Caserio himself is taking a more grassroots approach.

"Texans GM Nick Caserio is at today's Houston opener," the Houston Chronicle's Joseph Duarte first reported on X on September 5, which prompted a fan to drop photographic evidence.

— Melissa Balcom (@MelissaBalcom) September 5, 2026

The proximity–the University of Houston is less than 15 minutes away from the Texans' headquarters at NRG Park–affords Caserio and Co. ample opportunities to see both Cougars prospects and those from visiting schools.

There are several that will be active in this contest, and on both sides.

Two of the more intriguing Cougars prospects are, as it is for Ohio State, at quarterback and wide receiver, where Conner Wiegman and Amare Thomas are drawing attention, respectively ahead of the 2027 draft.

"Amare Thomas is a mid-level sleeper WR prospect with early-round upside and verifiable production," Pro Football Network wrote in its profile on the playmaker.

"At around 5'11", 204 pounds, Thomas is well-built with natural leverage and compact mass, and he's an incredibly fluid and twitched-up mover, with the short-area energy and quickness to off-set as a separator and create as a ball carrier. Functionally, Thomas has inside-outside versatility and a promising route tree."

Weigman is a polarizing but intriguing prospect at the QB spot.

Weigman was a five-star and the top-ranked quarterback in his class at Texas A&M before injuries and inconsistency derailed his time there," NFL Draft Buzz's Wyatt Brooks wrote in his profile on the QB. "He is a live-armed rhythm passer with a quick release and a flair for the clutch, with four game-winning drives on the season.

"The five-star tools and the late-season poise are the reasons to bet on him, even as the extensive medical history demands a long look."

The Texans are good at QB1 with C.J. Stroud through at least 202, barring a sudden change of heart. However, their backup situation is far less certain. Current QB2 Davis Mills is in a contract year, while intended QB3 Graham Mertz is out for the season after tearing his ACL during a preseason game.

It was Mertz's second torn ACL.

He will be in Year 3, without any regular-season experience come 2027, which is why Weigman could be interesting to the Texans.

The Cougars have other pros to keep an eye on. NFL Mock Draft Database lists interior offensive lineman Shadre Hurst and Anthony Boswell, running back Makhi Hughes, and wide receiver Trent Walker as options, all with Day 3 projections.

There are fewer prospects on the Beavers' side.

NFL Mock Draft Database projects offensive tackle Teko Shoats and quarterback Maalik Murphy could be taken at some point during the 2027 cycle, perhaps even by Caserio and the Texans.

title: From chess to battle for pole, Gasly has Russell covered at Monza
description: Pierre Gasly delivered the biggest surprise pole position in F1 for years in Italy as the leading contenders had scrappy qualifying sessions.
fullText:
A quarter of an hour before the qualifying session which delivered the biggest surprise pole position in Formula 1 for years, Alpine's Pierre Gasly was playing online chess with Mercedes driver George Russell and winning.

"I must say before the quali, I felt pretty confident," the Frenchman said, "because I was picking piece by piece after piece."

Gasly's performance coach Ben Thorne was watching.

"For a fun story," Gasly said, "Ben told me, 'OK, well, you're getting George here, but he's going to get you in a few minutes.'"

Gasly said he reacted with a swear word but he was smiling as he recalled the moment.

"Turned out that it worked out well. So yeah, it's been fun," he added.

Russell, who lines up second to Gasly, was laughing about it. "He beat me there," the Briton said, "and I thought, 'Well, I think I'll beat you in qualifying,' and here we are, he's ahead of me again."

No-one - especially not Gasly nor his Alpine team - would have predicted the 30-year-old would end up on pole in Monza on Saturday, even though his only win in F1 came at this exact track six years ago.

That victory, in the middle of F1's bizarre, spectator-less pandemic season, owed a lot to luck - a remarkable race that ended up with Gasly, then driving for Red Bull's Toro Rosso team, taking a restart from third place and Lance Stroll going off ahead of him on the first lap to gift him the lead once Lewis Hamilton had served a penalty.

This pole was not like that. It was absolutely earned on merit.

The Alpine has strong straight-line speed with a low-downforce-leaning aerodynamic design. The car - which has a Mercedes engine, the best in the field - has looked quick all weekend. It had an upgrade that lifted its performance at the last race in the Netherlands. And Gasly and his team absolutely nailed qualifying, while all the usual leading contenders had scrappy sessions one way or another.

"Monza is a bit of unique track as we know," Gasly said. "It definitely exceeded all our expectations.

"Since this morning, the pace has been better. We managed to make a good step from P3 to quali and I think slightly bigger than the other guys around us.

"Straight from Q1, we were a bit surprised to see us up there. Our target was Q3. But then I was P1 in Q1, then P4 in Q2. I didn't want to get too excited but then first run in Q3, I was third again.

"And then I felt, 'OK, well, I really have a shot at it.' It's probably the first time I really get a true chance and tried to leave everything I had out there.

"It was quite hectic through Ascari and Parabolica. I don't think there was definitely much (left) in there. And crossing the line, I knew it will be one of these laps that will be rewarded. But to the point to get to the pole position, I didn't expect that."

Alpine's Gasly beats Russell to stunning Monza pole

Gasly is well liked within the paddock, and has many friends among the drivers, but he has long been one of F1's forgotten heroes, regardless of that win six years ago.

A Red Bull protege, his time in the works team in 2019 did not work out. Like so many since, he was crushed by Max Verstappen, and demoted back to the second team after half a season.

After sticking with Red Bull for three more years, he was given an opportunity with Alpine, and he hoped a move to a factory team would be his making.

But Alpine have stumbled since, until finally showing signs of a revival this season, following Renault's decision to abandon its F1 engine project and switch to Mercedes customer engines.

The team had been making headlines already this weekend.

On Friday, Gasly lost the podium at Monaco to which he had been promoted after Alpine won an appeal against two penalties for pit-lane speeding, when the FIA court of appeal reinstated the punishment.

A few hours later, de facto team boss Flavio Briatore caused an eruption in a news conference when he alleged one of the four judges in the case had "links" with McLaren.

It was a claim that appeared to lack any substance, based as it was on a charity event in California in 2018 at which the judge in question had been present and to which a local McLaren garage had apparently donated "two or three" cars.

And Briatore provided no evidence to back up the insinuation he was making.

The claim was described as "insulting" in that news conference by McLaren team principal Andrea Stella, and afterwards it became clear that McLaren were furious about what Briatore had said on apparently the most flimsy of bases.

Then, on Saturday, a rare statement from the FIA court of appeal refuted the allegation and any "questions (about) the independence and impartiality of the judges".

The court of appeal verdict made a lot of sense. It left many questions about the controversy of the pit-lane penalties in Monaco, but at least it ensured all drivers who had been given them had been treated equitably - notwithstanding the fact that it seems none of them should have received the penalties.

Regardless of the questionable nature of Briatore's comments, Alpine were unhappy about losing their Monaco podium, feeling that they had been given two penalties unjustly when their evidence showed Gasly had never been over the pit-lane speeding limit.

Managing director Steve Nielsen told Sky Sports: "Two or three days ago, we were on the floor. It is really from being down to being on top of the world in just two days and it is amazing. We need to soak it up and make the best of it.

"Pierre is a class act. If you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year.

"We haven't always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have, he has delivered, particularly earlier in the season, So to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful."

In qualifying, Gasly was positioned second last in the train of cars on the final qualifying run, the absolute optimum place in terms of a slipstream.

Others, meanwhile, were compromised in one way or another, including the favourite for pole, Russell, when Verstappen disrupted Mercedes' attempts to have team-mate Kimi Antonelli tow the Briton by getting between the two silver cars at the end of their out laps.

"We had a bit of a mess with Verstappen entering the lap," Russell said. "He wanted to go for the tow, Kimi was there as well, and I did my lap a second and a half behind Max, which wasn't ideal.

"It takes nothing away from what Pierre achieved because, as he said, they were flying all day, quickest in Q1 and right up there from the beginning. So I'm happy for Pierre and, of course, disappointed we weren't on pole ourselves. However, great place to start for tomorrow."

Russell acknowledged after qualifying what is at stake for him on Sunday. He goes into the race 59 championship points behind leader Antonelli, who has pretty much had his measure all season. But he has a golden opportunity to make up ground on the Italian, who is due to start 20th because of a grid penalty for exceeding his engine allowance.

Russell said: "The win is going to be very important tomorrow but I'm more pleased about the performance. Since the summer break, every lap I have been in the top three positions, while I had that tough run of form before the break when every lap wasn't in the top five."

Antonelli is expected easily to get back into the top six or so, but that would still allow Russell to make a substantial dent in his advantage.

Given Russell has his own grid penalty looming within a couple of races for the same reason, it is imperative for his title hopes that he does so.

On Friday, Gasly did not appear to have the race speed to challenge the top teams, so even though overtaking is harder at Monza than might be expected given its long straights, he knows it will be tough to win the race.

"Obviously not to the pace of these guys around us, but we seem to have picked up more pace from yesterday to today," Gasly said. "So we'll obviously give our best shot and see what we can get out of it."

Aside from Gasly, Russell's main opposition is likely to come from Ferrari, who for the third race in a row seemed to fumble a better qualifying result for operational reasons. It was a bad time to do it again, as they debuted their upgraded engine at their home race.

After both cars came perilously close to being knocked out in the second part of qualifying, Charles Leclerc left the pits in the final session while Lewis Hamilton had no wheels on his car, so the seven-time champion was far from best placed for his run in terms of the slipstream.

Leclerc and Hamilton will start third and fourth after McLaren's Oscar Piastri was given a three-place grid penalty for impeding Red Bull's Liam Lawson.

Hamilton - like Russell, 59 points behind Antonelli - seemed to imply after qualifying that he felt the team should prioritise his hopes over Leclerc's, even if he could not quite bring himself to say it outright.

"(Piastri's penalty) puts us in (with a) fighting chance, hopefully, with George," Hamilton said. "That's one Mercedes up front, so hopefully that gives us a chance to work as a team to try and topple them.

"We're at a point in the year where 59 points is a huge - huge - deficit to recover from, especially when Mercedes continue to be the leaders in speed.

"So yeah, we do have to work as a team. Have we been... if and when that would ever change... we'll find out, but all I can do is just try to arrive and do the best job I can."

title: Who is Indiana football’s backup quarterback? Meet Grant Wilson
description: Indiana football backup Grant Wilson has entered the game against North Texas. Here's what to know about the veteran:
fullText:
BLOOMINGTON — Indiana football backup quarterback Grant Wilson made his 2026 debut Saturday in the fourth quarter of his team's season opener.

Wilson's first game reps came with IU leading 45-16 over North Texas. He scored on the first snap. It was the first time he played since a Week 10 win over Maryland in 2025.

The veteran quarterback won the backup job for the Hoosiers in fall camp over Tyler Cherry. Here's what to know about Wilson:

More: IU's Curt Cignetti keeps sideline reporters on their toes. They wouldn't want it any other way

When Cignetti's staff landed in Bloomington, Wilson was a familiar name in the transfer portal.

The former Old Dominion starter faced off against Cignetti's JMU team in 2023 and nearly ended the program's 10-0 start. Wilson threw for 277 yards (26 of 36) and two touchdowns in the 30-27 loss.

Wilson threw a go-ahead score in the fourth quarter of the game that was overturned on replay.

More: Big Noon crew praises IU football's blueprint for developing transfer QBs

Wilson suffered a devastating arm injury during a Week 2 loss to East Carolina in 2024. He dislocated his elbow, tore a tendon in his tricep and another one in his wrist.

While rehabbing the injury after the season, Wilson received offers to compete for a starting job from Group of Five teams when he entered the transfer portal. Indiana also expressed interest in having him to Bloomington in what essentially amounted to a mentor role for the Mendoza brothers.

"It's hard to turn down Curt Cignetti," Wilson told The Herald-Times in 2025. "Just listening to his pitch and seeing what he did from Elon to JMU, the 2024 season. It's unreal, hard to deny the success he had."

More: Why Urban Meyer believes Indiana football has key advantage in quest for repeat titles

As IU's third-string quarterback, Wilson dedicated much of his energy to helping Fernando Mendoza and his brother. Wilson would spend extra time watching film with Fernando and offer him immediate feedback on reps during practice.

"He's like a full-time quarterback fundamental coach," Mendoza told The Herald-Times in 2025.

Then Indiana quarterbacks coach Chandler Whitmer appreciated Wilson's efforts as well.

"It's nice to have another voice in there that's aligned with what I'm teaching, and obviously in the meetings every single day and be another voice for Fernando as a peer," Whitmer said. "Grant has been great, I can't say enough good things."

More: How Indiana football QB Josh Hoover found his way back to Bloomington

Wilson wants to get into coaching, but he delayed those pursuits when the NCAA granted his waiver for a seventh season of eligibility. He returned to Bloomington and won the backup job over Tyler Cherry during fall camp.

"I would say Grant definitely has the edge for the number two," Cignetti said. "He's an experienced guy, and he's had a good camp. And Tyler's improved, too."

Wilson has thrown for 2,661 yards with 21 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 18 games at the FBS level. At Fordham from 2021-22, he threw for 93 yards and two scores.

Michael Niziolek is the Indiana beat reporter for The Bloomington Herald-Times. You can follow him on X @michaelniziolek.

fullText:

"During the game, we tried to feel comfortable, create some good individual actions and be clinical. We created around five good chances to score. The next step for us is to continue building the team and try to correct a few things offensively. We are improving, but not enough.

"Overall, I can tell the fans and the players that I understand this is the way. In the last four years, with the success and performances we have had, we have had some days like today."

On new players taking time to gel: "The players who joined us need some adaption. Some our adapting quicker than others. In everything we are building, we must try and add the players who joined us in the direction we want."

title: Ohio State stars were out as Jeremiah Smith, Julian Sayin, Bo Jackson excel for Buckeyes
description: The top-ranked team in the nation relied on its star trio of returning starters.
fullText:
It's never too early for the Heisman Trophy hype machine to crank up, and Ohio State left Week 1 of the college football season with a trio of attractive candidates in a romp over Ball State.

Junior wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, who finished sixth in Heisman voting last year, continued to prove that he's a lock to be a top-five NFL Draft pick. Smith led the Buckeyes with eight catches for 161 yards (both game highs) and two eye-popping touchdown receptions.

Quarterback Julian Sayin, a 2025 Heisman finalist, rebounded from a disappointing exit from last year's College Football Playoff by completing 21 of 25 passes for 320 yards and no interceptions (a rating of 231.1).

Running back Bo Jackson (who already has a Heisman-worthy moniker) ripped off a 65-yard touchdown while rushing nine times for 83 yards (not to be outdone, teammate Ja'Kobi Jackson also rushed for 83 yards, including a 48-yard TD).

It's a long way to the December awards presentation in New York, and there already have been some other impressive performances in Week 1, but the Buckeyes are at least on the Heisman board with their star trio of returning starters.

title: Giants’ DJ Reader Gets Blunt on Pressure to Replace Dexter Lawrence
description: The New York Giants made the tough decision this offseason to replace one of their best and longest-tenured players, defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence.After seven seasons, three Pro Bowl nods, and two second-team All-Pro honors, the former 17th overall pick and the team that drafted him were unable to find common ground on an extension, and […] The post Giants’ DJ Reader Gets Blunt on Pressure to Replace Dexter Lawrence appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The New York Giants made the tough decision this offseason to replace one of their best and longest-tenured players, defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence.

After seven seasons, three Pro Bowl nods, and two second-team All-Pro honors, the former 17th overall pick and the team that drafted him were unable to find common ground on an extension, and the Giants traded him to the Cincinnati Bengals, netting a first-round draft pick.

To replace him, New York turned to the free-agent market, inking veteran names like DJ Reader and Shelby Harris to replace Lawrence in the aggregate.

It's never going to be easy replacing a former All-Pro-caliber player, but Reader told the New York Post's Steve Serby he's going to do his best despite his different skill set from Lawrence.

In the interview with the New York Post, Serby asked Reader about the pressure he's facing in replacing such a talented player on the New York Giants, but the 10-year veteran is ignoring the outside noise and focusing on himself.

"I put a tremendous amount of pressure on myself as a player, especially in the run game. Obviously there's pressures from the outside, but I don't pay attention to 'em as much. I feel very confident in me being to do the job I came here to do. Not gonna be that player, not looking to be Dex, he plays the game a little bit different than the way I play it, but I feel like we both do it effectively," Reader told Serby.

"We affect the game. We affect the quarterback, we affect the run game. The thing is a special way that I do it, and I've been doing it for a long time at a high level in my position. So I would just say you're getting a physical player who's really bought into the system and is gonna play his ass off."

While Reader is certainly a great player in his own right, he doesn't have the career accolades a player like Lawrence has to his name. That doesn't mean he can't be impactful, though, and in some areas on defense, the former Detroit Lions defensive tackle is actually better.

Lawrence was an elite pass rusher for the New York Giants over the last seven years of his career. He recorded a grand total of 30.5 sacks, which is a lot for a defensive tackle.

But he always seemed to struggle against the run, which has been the Giants' biggest defensive weakness over the last few seasons.

Just last season, New York gave up 145.3 rushing yards per game, 31st-worst across the entire league.

Reader, who carries a reputation as a staunch run defender, is hoping to change that in 2026.

Serby asked the veteran defensive tackle if the Giants will be able to stop the run this season in the interview, and Reader gave a short but stern answer.

"Yeah, I confidently believe so. We gotta go out there and do it, but I believe so."

We'll see if Reader and Big Blue's new-look defense can pull it off.

title: Report card for Indiana football's win over North Texas
description: Indiana football beat North Texas in its season opener, time to hand out grades.
fullText:
BLOOMINGTON — Indiana football beat North Texas 52-16 to open the 2026 season on Saturday at Memorial Stadium.

Outside a strong debut for quarterback Josh Hoover, it wasn't the prettiest of victories, but the No. 6 Hoosiers still managed to pull away in the second half and win comfortably.

Here's a report card for Saturday's win:

More: How Indiana football QB Josh Hoover found his way back to Bloomington

The running game looked stuck in neutral, but that didn't matter with Josh Hoover throwing dimes all game long. He had an impressive debut, and did a nice job of taking advantage of his various weapons. Indiana had seven players with at least one catch, including a tight end and running back. The early signs of chemistry he showed with Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh were encouraging as well.

The defense's film review session with Bryant Haines in the coming days won't be pretty. Indiana has a lot to clean up — the tackling wasn't good — and players will definitely hear about North Texas converting nearly half of its third down attempts. The Mean Green even converted a third-and-23 to extend a drive late in the third quarter.

The Hoosiers do get credit for twice holding North Texas to field goals in the red zone and it's worth noting both their starting corners were knocked out of the game well before halftime.

Nico Radicic set a career-high with a 49-yard field goal, and IU had a pair of long kickoff returns in the first half that set up easy touchdown drives. The Hoosiers special teams units have often been an overlooked part of IU's success over the last two seasons, but the amount of winning plays they make every game adds up. Radicic boosting his range in the offseason will pay dividends throughout the season.

With the shadow of Fernando Mendoza looming large, the shot of a bloodied Hoover throwing a touchdown pass to Becker was an important moment. This is now his offense, and the toughness he put on display for his teammeates and fans showed he's up to the challenge.

title: FCS program Tarleton State stuns Bowling Green in Week 1 shocker
description: Tarleton State continued its climb by beating another FBS team, taking down Bowling Green for the first FCS over FBS win of 2026.
fullText:
It didn't take long for the first FCS upset to happen in the 2026 college football season.

FCS heavyweight Tarleton State beat Bowling Green 20-13 in Week 1, and while the score indicates it was a close one, there was no fluke in the Texans' win.

Tarleton State pounced on the Falcons off the jump, going right into the endzone on its opening drive to take a 7-0 lead. The offense was consistent, and after a 99-yard touchdown drive late in the second quarter, Tarleton State was up a commanding 17-0.

REQUIRED READING: Lane Kiffin says 'uncertainties' led him to leave ex-NFL players off LSU roster

Bowling Green was able to find the endzone before halftime and made it a one-score game in the fourth quarter with a chance to tie, but the Falcons were stopped on fourth down with two minutes to go. On the ensuing play, running back Tylan Hines broke off an 82-yard run as he amassed a 250-yard day.

The Falcons were able to get the ball back, but unable to get the game-tying score with Tarleton State getting a wire-to-wire win.

Even though it's an FCS team, Tarelton State is one of the best teams at the level under 17th-year coach Todd Whitten. It is located in Stephenville, Texas, about 90 miles southwest of Dallas.

It is coming off 12-2 season, where it was the the United Athletic Conference co-champion and made the FCS playoff quarterfinals. It is the ranked No. 5 in the FCS rankings, and opened the season with a win over Prairie View A&M.

The Texans are no strangers to upsets, as this is the second straight season it has beaten an FCS team after it took down Army in a double overtime thriller last season, becoming the 16th FCS team since 2006 to win back-to-back games against FBS opponents.

It also further strengthens the case for Tarleton State to continue its climb in college football.

Even though Tarleton State moved up to FCS in 2020, it's already generating support to move up to the FBS level. Athletic director Steve Uryasz confirmed the plans to Front Office Sports in August, as the university has spent tens of millions of dollars on athletics, including renovating its stadium, increasing its budget to over $40 million and participating in revenue-sharing.

While the future is not decided, Tarleton State is becoming one of the top teams in FCS.

title: Defenses worth prioritizing in 2026 fantasy football drafts
description: If you're going to use a premium pick on a D/ST, here are your options
fullText:
Defenses are often overlooked in fantasy football drafts, and understandably so. Hunting matchups via streaming defenses is certainly a viable strategy, even though it requires plenty of waiver wire due diligence.

Still, the comfort of week-to-week consistency that an elite defense brings is underrated. It could give you a unique matchup advantage akin to having a standout tight end.

While this is by no means a case against streaming defenses, here are five units worth prioritizing in 2026 fantasy football drafts if you do decide to dedicate a premium pick to it.

DeMeco Ryans' defense is the NFL's best, full of hard-hitters and a turnovers machine in cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. Houston also has one of the 10 easiest schedules, so matchups are in its favor as well.

The Eagles are loaded to the brim with defensive talent, particularly in the front seven with standouts like Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis. Getting to play the Washington Commanders, who have one of the NFL's worst offensive lines, twice is year is also an advantage.

Denver comfortably led the NFL in sacks a season ago and is well-positioned to finish atop the league again. If Sean Payton's offense can take another leap, it'll lead to more passing downs for the defense, which means plenty more opportunities for sacks and interceptions.

Mike Macdonald has a strong case to be the NFL's top defensive mind, and he has the exact right personnel to realize his vision in Seattle. The Seahawks' young secondary, led by second-year safety Nick Emmanwori, is one of the most league's most fun groups to watch.

Aaron Donald came out of retirement to join Myles Garrett on the Rams. That's a combined 17 Pro Bowls and five Defensive Player of the Year awards. Need I say more?

title: Oli Marmol ejected after umpire told rookie pitcher to fix hat
description: St. Louis Cardinals manager Oli Marmol was ejected during Friday's victory over the Colorado Rockies after arguing with home-plate umpire Doug Eddings, shorty after Eddings apparently told rookie pitcher Hancel Rincon to straighten his hat.
fullText:
DENVER - St. Louis Cardinals manager Oli Marmol was ejected during Friday's victory over the Colorado Rockies after arguing with home-plate umpire Doug Eddings, shorty after Eddings apparently told rookie pitcher Hancel Rincon to straighten his hat.

Rincon made his MLB debut in the sixth inning of Friday's contest with the Cardinals leading the Rockies 4-1 at the time.

Early into his outing, Eddings reportedly instructed Rincon to straighten his cap, which was slightly tilted toward the left.

According to reports from several MLB media members, Eddings claimed Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman brought the titled hat to his attention.

Rincon adjusted his hat and retired Goodman, but ran into trouble after that. The next three hitters reached based, and the Rockies cut the deficit to 4-3 with one out before Justin Bruihl replaced Rincon on the mound.

During the pitching change, Marmol confronted Eddings about the remarks made to Rincon. The two continued talking for several minutes with Marmol visibly upset about how the message had been delivered to the rookie pitcher.

Before too long, Marmol was ejected.

According to MLB.com's Owen Perkins and Brenden Schaefer, Marmol shared his side of the story afterward.

"I had an issue with Doug. Just Doug. He took it upon himself to tell our rookie pitcher the kid's 'not going to wear his hat on my field that way.' You got Dontrelle Willis, CC Sabathia, Pedro Strop, plenty of guys that have worn it way more tilted. I have an issue with that. That's just a power-hungry move, in my opinion."

"Quite honestly, I thought it was pretty embarrassing on his end. We have a kid making his debut and in between an at-bat he tells him that he needs to fix his hat and the kid's not going to wear his hat like that on my field."

"I took issue with it. And then the pitch violation while I'm out there having the discussion, that's also stupid, in my opinion. "

"There's a lot of moving parts to that one. At the end of the day, I thought they handled it poorly and I'd like an explanation at some point."

The game unraveled for a moment after Marmol's ejection.

Eddings added a ball onto the next hitter's count, ruling that Marmol's argument had caused a pace-of-play disruption. The Rockies then strung together several quality at-bats to take a 5-4 lead.

On the go-ahead run, Eddings ruled Colorado's Troy Johnston safe on a bang-bang play at the plate. Replay appeared to show Cardinals catcher Leo Bernal may have applied the tag before Johnston touched home, but the call ultimately stood.

The Cardinals then trailed 6-4 heading into the ninth inning, but designated hitter Ivan Herrera played hero. With one out, Herrera hit a go-ahead, three-run home run that held up for the victory.

The ejection marked Marmol's fourth this season, and he is expected to receive a fine.

The Cardinals improved to 71-71 with the victory and enter Saturday just three games out of the National League's final Wild Card spot. Twenty games remain in the Cardinals' 2026 regular season.

title: Serhou Guirassy extends his run and draws level with a BVB legend
description: For the past two years, the 30-year-old striker has been lighting it up for Borussia Dortmund. And he is on fire (again). Two games, two goals in this still-young season. Next Tuesday, he could make h...
fullText:
For the past two years, the 30-year-old striker has been lighting it up for Borussia Dortmund. And he is on fire (again). Two games, two goals in this still-young season. Next Tuesday, he could make his 100th competitive appearance for the Black and Yellows. After 99 matches, he has an incredible 62 goals to his name. Only Erling Haaland and Lothar Emmerich have bettered that return.

Haaland scored an outstanding 86 goals in just 89 competitive matches for BVB. Lothar Emmerich found the net 64 times in his first 100 Bundesliga games for Borussia Dortmund.

Back to Guirassy. The Guinean now has 40 Bundesliga goals in Black and Yellow — the same number as Norbert Dickel scored. One small difference: Guirassy needed 65 games to get there, Dickel 90.

In the 3-2 away win at Hoffenheim, Guirassy was involved in six of Dortmund's eight shots on goal. In the 61st minute, he scored to make it 1-2, and five minutes later he set up Fabio Silva for the 2-2 equalizer. That means Serhou Guirassy has now scored exactly one goal in each of his last five away games at TSG. (br)
